items.title: Tyson Stock At $59: Is Immigration Raising Your Grocery Bill?
items.summary: Pick up a pack of ground beef this weekend and look at the sticker. In October, beef prices at the store rose 0.9% in a single month, more than twice the 0.4% rise in all consumer prices. Here is the odd part: the company that packs much of that beef is losing money on it. Tyson Foods expected its beef business to lose $625 million to $775 million in the fiscal year that just ended, citing one of the most severe cattle shortages in U.S. history.
